conventions.commits: Conventional Commits with feat/fix/docs/refactor/test/chore scopes; GPG-signed with --signoff (DCO required)
conventions.testing: Unit tests in language module files (mod tests block); integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs; test patterns: parse_and_query helper, tree traversal with stack, SemanticExtractor for defuse sites
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings (deny: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used with test exemptions), cargo deny check advisories licenses
conventions.error_handling: thiserror for custom error types, Option<T> for fallible operations, bounds checking on source byte ranges (end_byte() <= source.len())

patterns: Language modules live in crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/<lang>.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY constants
Each language registers in get_language_info() match arm in mod.rs with LanguageInfo struct containing queries and optional handler functions
Handler functions (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance) take &Node and &str source, return Option<String> or Vec<String>
Extension map in lang.rs maps file extensions to language identifiers; language_for_extension() used for dispatch
Tree-sitter grammar dependency added to Cargo.toml workspace.dependencies with pinned version; crate-level dependency in aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml
Tests verify query compilation, node traversal, handler correctness, and defuse site extraction via SemanticExtractor

constraints: All languages unconditionally compiled in (lang-* feature gates removed in #1235)
tree-sitter-php crate must be added to workspace.dependencies with pinned version
DEFUSE_QUERY is required for languages with identifier tracking (write/read sites); optional for markup languages
Inheritance extraction walks parent nodes to find extends/implements clauses; field names vary by grammar
Query strings are raw strings (r#"..."#) to avoid escaping tree-sitter syntax
test_coverage: Language modules include unit tests for query compilation, node extraction, and handler functions. Integration tests in integration_tests.rs verify end-to-end parsing and element extraction. Java tests cover: extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, element_query_happy_path, extract_inheritance, defuse_query_write_site. Similar coverage expected for PHP.

library_findings.relevant_api: Language constant tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE; node types: class_declaration (fields: name, body, attributes), interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration, method_declaration, function_definition; inheritance via base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) as sibling nodes, not fields
library_findings.notes: PHP grammar uses base_clause and class_interface_clause as separate child nodes (not fields) to carry inheritance info; class_declaration.name is a 'name' node type; method_declaration and function_definition both exist; no parent_class/interfaces fields like Java

library_findings.relevant_api: Query::new(), QueryCursor, Node::child_by_field_name(), Node::named_child(), Node::parent(), Node::start_byte(), Node::end_byte(), Node::kind()
library_findings.notes: Core API for tree-sitter parsing and node traversal; bounds checking required on byte ranges

approaches.name: Full PHP handler with all optional features
approaches.description: Add php.rs module with ELEMENT_QUERY covering class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration, method_declaration, function_definition; CALL_QUERY for function_call_expression; REFERENCE_QUERY for qualified_name; IMPORT_QUERY for namespace_use_declaration; DEFUSE_QUERY for local variable and assignment tracking; implement extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance handlers. Wire in mod.rs get_language_info() and get_ts_language() match arms, add tree-sitter-php to Cargo.toml, add 'php' to lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP with '.php' extension, add 'php' to supported_languages(), write comprehensive unit and integration tests.
pros: Maximum feature parity with Java/Kotlin implementations
Enables full semantic extraction: inheritance, method receivers, defuse sites
Comprehensive test coverage catches edge cases
cons: Largest implementation effort (~400-500 LOC for module + tests)
Requires deep understanding of PHP grammar structure
More complex handler logic for inheritance (base_clause/class_interface_clause navigation)

approaches.name: Minimal PHP handler (queries only, no handlers)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, and DEFUSE_QUERY constants only; register in mod.rs with all handler fields set to None; wire extension map and supported_languages. Skip extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance implementations. Minimal tests verify query compilation only.
pros: Sufficient for basic symbol extraction and call graph analysis
cons: No method receiver type resolution (impacts call graph accuracy)
No inheritance extraction (misses class hierarchy analysis)

approaches.name: Phased approach: queries first, handlers in follow-up
approaches.description: Phase 1 (this PR): Add php.rs with all query constants and register in mod.rs/lang.rs with None handlers; comprehensive query tests. Phase 2 (follow-up issue): Implement extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance handlers with inheritance walk tests. Allows landing PHP support quickly and iterating on handler quality.
pros: Allows community feedback on queries before handler complexity
Separates concerns: parsing vs semantic analysis
cons: Requires two PRs instead of one

recommendation: Approach 1 (Full PHP handler with all optional features). The issue explicitly references modeling after Java, and the codebase shows that language integrations are expected to include handler functions for production use (see Swift #1742, Kotlin #800). The PHP grammar's base_clause/class_interface_clause pattern is well-defined and navigable. Full implementation provides immediate value for inheritance analysis and method resolution, aligns with project quality standards, and avoids technical debt from incomplete handlers. The complexity is justified by the precedent and the benefit.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}

inheritance_walk_citation: For a class_declaration node, walk child nodes to find base_clause (contains 'extends' keyword followed by _name nodes) and class_interface_clause (contains 'implements' keyword followed by _name nodes). Extract text from each _name child node. base_clause structure per grammar.js: seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)). class_interface_clause structure: seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)). Neither is a field on class_declaration; both are sibling nodes in the declaration_list. Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js
